summary.goal:
Build a small key-value store CLI in this repository (Node.js, ES modules, no dependencies).

Entry point: bin/kv.js, run as `node bin/kv.js <command> [args] [--file <path>]`. The store is a JSON file; `--file` selects it and defaults to `.kv.json` in the current directory. Writes must be atomic (write a temporary file, then rename).

Commands:
- `set <key> <value...>`: stores the value (all remaining arguments joined with single spaces). Prints nothing, exit code 0. Optional `--ttl <seconds>` makes the key expire that many seconds after it was set.
- `get <key>`: prints the value followed by a newline, exit code 0. For a missing or expired key prints `not found: <key>` on stderr and exits with code 1. An expired key is removed from the file when it is read.
- `del <key>`: removes the key and prints `deleted`, exit 0; for a missing key prints `not found: <key>` on stderr and exits 1.
- `list`: prints every non-expired key, sorted, one per line; prints nothing for an empty store.

Keys must match /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/; otherwise print `invalid key: <key>` on stderr and exit 1. An unknown command prints usage on stderr and exits 2.

Add tests in test/ using node:test that run the CLI as a child process against a temporary file and cover every command, the error cases and TTL expiry (use a short TTL and a fake clock or an already-expired timestamp; the file stores absolute expiry times in milliseconds). Add a "test" script to package.json so that `npm test` runs them, and write a README.md that documents every command. npm test must pass.

tasks.title: Implement the kv store CLI (store module, command logic, entry point)
tasks.spec:
Implement the whole CLI in one pull request, exactly per the design document: the store file format, the atomic write rule, the expiry model, argument parsing, exit codes and output strings are all frozen there.

Deliverables:
- src/store.js: KEY_PATTERN, isValidKey, emptyStore, isExpired, loadStore, saveStore, pruneExpired, listKeys with the documented signatures. loadStore returns an empty store when the file is missing and throws an Error with code 'ESTOREFORMAT' when the file exists but is not valid JSON or not a JSON object. saveStore serializes with JSON.stringify(store, null, 2) + '\n', creates missing parent directories, writes to <basename>.tmp-<pid>-<random> in the same directory, then renames it over the target, removing the temp file on failure.
- src/cli.js: USAGE, run(argv, { now = Date.now() } = {}) returning the exit code, and main(argv) assigning process.exitCode. Implements set/get/del/list, the global --file flag, the set-only --ttl flag, key validation, usage on exit-2 paths, and the exact stdout/stderr strings and exit codes from the design. Synchronous only; no process.exit(); no async/await.
- bin/kv.js: shebang, a single import of main from ../src/cli.js, and the call.

Boundaries: do not create test files and do not edit package.json or README.md (tasks cli-tests and readme own those). No dependencies. Every stdout/stderr write ends with a newline. Do ad-hoc checks with `node bin/kv.js ...` against files in /tmp; never leave a .kv.json in the project root.

commands: node bin/kv.js set greeting "hello world" --file /tmp/kv-accept-a.json && test "$(node bin/kv.js get greeting --file /tmp/kv-accept-a.json)" = "hello world"
node bin/kv.js set k1 v1 --file /tmp/kv-accept-b.json && node bin/kv.js del k1 --file /tmp/kv-accept-b.json && test -z "$(node bin/kv.js list --file /tmp/kv-accept-b.json)"
node bin/kv.js set eph val --ttl 0.1 --file /tmp/kv-accept-d.json && sleep 0.5 && node bin/kv.js get eph --file /tmp/kv-accept-d.json 2>/dev/null; test $? -eq 1
acceptance.review: Confirm by reading the code and by ad-hoc runs that: writes are atomic (temp file in the same directory, rename, no leftovers after set/del); get and del on an expired key print 'not found: <key>' to stderr, exit 1 and remove the entry from the file, while a never-existing key does not create or rewrite the file; list prints sorted non-expired keys and never writes; an invalid key prints 'invalid key: <key>' and exits 1; an unparseable store file prints 'cannot read store: <path>' and exits 1 without modifying it; --file works before or after the command; --ttl accepts fractional seconds and rejects non-numeric or negative values; every stdout/stderr write ends with a newline.

report.summary: Implemented the whole kv CLI, exactly to the frozen design, in the three files in my scope: src/store.js (KEY_PATTERN, isValidKey, emptyStore, isExpired, loadStore, saveStore, pruneExpired, listKeys), src/cli.js (USAGE, run(argv, { now = Date.now() }) returning 0/1/2, main(argv) assigning process.exitCode), and bin/kv.js (shebang, one import, main()). Synchronous ESM only, no dependencies, no process.exit(), no async/await. Argument parsing is a single left-to-right pass where --file and --ttl each consume the next token and every other token (including ones starting with '-') is positional. set joins the remaining arguments with single spaces, prunes expired entries and saves atomically; get prints the value or reports 'not found: <key>' on stderr with exit 1 after removing an expired entry; del prints 'deleted' or the same not-found error; list prints sorted non-expired keys and never writes. Writes go through saveStore: mkdir -p the parent, write JSON.stringify(store, null, 2) + '\n' to <basename>.tmp-<pid>-<random> in the same directory, rename over the target, unlink the temp file on failure. Verified with the five harness acceptance commands (all exit 0) plus 119 ad-hoc assertions across spawned CLI runs and direct module-level checks with an injected fake clock.

Acceptance run from the project root, all five commands exit 0: acc1=0 (set/get 'hello world' via --file), acc2=0 (set, del, empty list), acc3=0 (get absent exits 1, and /tmp/kv-accept-c.json was never created), acc4=0 (frobnicate exits 2), acc5=0 (--ttl 0.1 then sleep 0.5, get exits 1). Extra verification: a 38-assertion bash sweep (default .kv.json in cwd with the exact pretty-printed format and trailing newline 0a; values joined and '-x -y' stored as a value; nested dirs created; zero temp files left after set/del; get and del on a never-existing key leave the store's shasum AND mtime unchanged; expired key prints 'not found: <key>' on stderr, exits 1, and the entry is gone from the file for both get and del while a live sibling key survives; list sorted code-unit order 'A _ a b', empty store prints nothing; invalid keys exit 1 with the exact message; 'not json', '[1,2]', '""' and an empty file all exit 1 with 'cannot read store: <path>' leaving the file byte-identical; hand-edited tolerance drops non-object/non-string-value entries and normalizes a non-numeric expiresAt). A 53-assertion second sweep (--file before and after the command; fractional ttl accepted, non-numeric/negative/Infinity rejected with 'invalid ttl: <value>' exit 1, ttl 0 expires immediately, --ttl on get/del/list is usage exit 2, missing or empty --file/--ttl values are exit 2; no-command and every wrong arity exit 2 with the exact USAGE text on stderr and nothing on stdout; plain set clears a previous expiry; set prunes expired entries; list with all keys expired prints nothing and does not rewrite the file; stdout is byte-exact 'v
', 'deleted
', 'a2
b2
'; a read-only directory makes the write fail with exit 1 and leaves no temp file). A 28-assertion module check imported src/store.js and src/cli.js directly: isExpired boundary (expiresAt <= now), pruneExpired returns the removal count and is idempotent, listKeys filters and sorts, loadStore returns { keys: {} } for a missing file without creating it and throws code ESTOREFORMAT for corrupt/array/string payloads, run(['set','k','v','--ttl','2.5'], { now: T0 }) writes expiresAt === T0 + 2500, get at T0+2499 prints 'v
' with exit 0 and at T0+2500 returns 1 with 'not found: k
' and prunes the entry, USAGE starts with the usage line and ends with 'list
'. Byte-level xxd checks confirmed every stderr message (usage, not found, invalid key, invalid ttl, cannot read store) ends in exactly one newline. git status shows only untracked bin/ and src/, with no .kv.json left in the project root.
decisions: Error precedence: usage/exit-2 paths win (unknown or missing command, wrong positional count, --ttl with a non-set command, missing or empty flag value), then key validation ('invalid key', 1), then ttl validation ('invalid ttl', 1). The design leaves the overlap of these cases unspecified.

loadStore maps any read failure other than ENOENT (EACCES, EISDIR, and the like) to the same ESTOREFORMAT path as invalid JSON, so the CLI reports 'cannot read store: <path>' with exit 1 instead of surfacing a raw Node stack trace. The design only spells out the invalid-JSON/invalid-object cases.

The --file value is passed to node:fs exactly as the user typed it, so fs resolves it against process.cwd() and the 'cannot read store: <path>' message echoes what the user wrote (the relative default stays '.kv.json') rather than an absolute path.
An empty-string flag value is treated as a missing value for both --file and --ttl (usage, exit 2); the design states this explicitly only for --file.
When a flag is repeated, the last occurrence wins. The design does not specify repetition.

del on an expired key removes the entry and saves before printing 'not found: <key>' and returning 1, matching the rule that get/del treat expired keys like missing ones while pruning them as a side effect.
An empty value is accepted and stored: `set key ""` writes value ''. Only the key is validated, and the design requires values to be strings, which '' is.
bin/kv.js carries the shebang from the design and was given the executable bit for convenience, although every documented invocation goes through `node bin/kv.js`.
openIssues: test/, package.json's scripts.test and README.md are owned by other tasks (cli-tests, readme), so `npm test` does not exist yet from my side; my verification used spawned CLI runs and direct module imports instead. The implementation is ready for the cli-tests suite to exercise.
I did not chmod the executable bit check into any test, and no .kv.json was left behind, so cli-tests can safely spawn the CLI with any working directory.

tasks.title: Automated node:test suite for the CLI plus the npm test script
tasks.spec:
Add the automated suite and wire it to npm, per the design's testing conventions. test/helpers.js exports tmpDir(), runKv(cwd, ...args) (spawnSync of process.execPath with bin/kv.js, encoding utf8, returning {status, stdout, stderr}) and readStore(file). The *.test.js files use node:test with node:assert/strict and spawn the CLI as a child process against a temporary file inside a directory from fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'kv-test-')). Never import src/ from a test and never run the CLI in the project root. Add {"scripts": {"test": "node --test test/*.test.js"}} to package.json; the explicit glob keeps test/helpers.js out of the run.

Required coverage: the set/get round trip including a multi-word value joined with single spaces, with exact stdout bytes; set prints nothing; set overwrites an existing key; get on a missing key writes 'not found: <key>' to stderr, nothing to stdout, exit 1; del prints 'deleted', exits 0, removes the key, and a repeat del exits 1; list is sorted one key per line, prints nothing for an empty store, and drops deleted keys; invalid keys for set/get/del (for example 'bad key', 'a/b', 'k!') print 'invalid key: <key>' and exit 1; an unknown command and no command print usage on stderr and exit 2; wrong positional counts exit 2; --file writes to the given path while an omitted --file writes .kv.json in the spawn cwd; the on-disk shape matches the frozen format ({ keys: { k: { value, expiresAt } } }); no temp files remain in the store directory after a write. TTL: seed a file with an already-past expiresAt and assert get and del treat it as missing and that get removes the entry from the file; seed a future expiresAt and assert get returns the value; assert an expired key is absent from list; include one short-TTL case ('--ttl 0.05', wait at least 200 ms, then get exits 1) and one '--ttl 60' case where the value is still readable; assert a negative or non-numeric --ttl exits 1. Keep at most one test that sleeps and give it a wide margin so the suite is not timing-fragile.

Detailed verification lives in these tests; the acceptance command is only the runner.

acceptance.review: Confirm the suite covers every command, every documented error path (exit 1 and exit 2), TTL expiry from both a seeded past timestamp and a short --ttl, atomic-write cleanup, and the --file default; confirm tests use only temp directories, that helpers.js is not collected as a test file, and that the suite is not timing-fragile (rerun it a few times).

report.summary:
Added the node:test suite and wired it into npm. Five new files under test/ (helpers.js plus four *.test.js suites, 46 tests) spawn bin/kv.js via spawnSync against a temp directory from fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir(), 'kv-test-') and assert on exact status/stdout/stderr bytes; package.json gained {"scripts":{"test":"node --test test/*.test.js"}}. `npm test` exits 0 in ~1.9 s.

Coverage: set/get round trip with a multi-word value joined by single spaces and exact stdout ('hello world again\n'), set prints nothing, set overwrites, get/list/del on a missing key (nothing on stdout, 'not found: <key>' on stderr, exit 1, and no store file created), del prints 'deleted', removes the key, repeat del exits 1, list is code-unit sorted one key per line and drops deleted keys, empty store lists nothing, invalid keys ('bad key', 'a/b', 'k!', '') for set/get/del, unknown command and no command print the exact usage text on stderr with exit 2, wrong positional counts exit 2, --ttl on a non-set command and missing/empty flag values exit 2, unknown flags-as-positional tokens, invalid JSON and non-object store files print 'cannot read store: <path>' with exit 1 and the file untouched, TTL from seeded past and future expiresAt (get/del treat expired as missing and prune the entry; list omits expired keys without rewriting the file), '--ttl 0' as a deterministic no-sleep expiry, one short-TTL case ('--ttl 0.05', 300 ms wait, get exits 1) as the only sleeping test, '--ttl 5'/'--ttl 60' readability with the on-disk expiry checked to be ≈ now+60000 ms, negative/non-numeric TTLs exit 1, the frozen on-disk shape with trailing newline, no temp files left after writes, --file in both positions, nested --file creating parent dirs, and the default .kv.json landing in the spawn cwd.

Verification: 5 clean `npm test` runs (46/46 pass), per-file counts 11+13+10+12 = 46 confirming helpers.js contributes no tests under the explicit glob while a bare `node --test` does collect it, and three mutation checks in a throwaway copy (/tmp, deleted afterwards) — changing 'deleted' to 'removed' failed 4 tests, joining values with '-' failed 3, reversing sort failed 3.
report.evidence: npm test -> "ℹ tests 46 / ℹ pass 46 / ℹ fail 0", exit 0, repeated 5 times (also under the full-file parallel run). node --test test/commands.test.js=11, errors=13, store-file=10, ttl=12, summing to the 46 of the glob run, so test/helpers.js is not collected; bare `node --test` prints "✔ test/helpers.js", which is why the explicit glob is required. Mutation checks on a copy at /tmp/kv-mut: stdout 'deleted'->'removed' => fail 4; valueParts.join(' ')->join('-') => fail 3; .sort()->.sort().reverse() => fail 3. git status shows only package.json modified plus the new test/ directory (bin/, src/, README.md belong to other tasks); no .kv.json, temp files, or other artifacts left in the project root.
decisions: One full run initially failed in the short-TTL test because I asserted the value was still readable immediately after `set --ttl 0.05`; a 50 ms window is too tight when four test files run in parallel. I removed that intermediate read and added a separate '--ttl 5' readability test, leaving exactly one sleeping test whose margin is 300 ms against a 50 ms TTL.

helpers.js exports a few things beyond the three required fixtures (BIN, USAGE, storePath, seedStore, assertRun) so the suites stay short; the exact usage text is duplicated there rather than imported from src/, since the design forbids tests importing src/.

Because the review asks for every documented error path, I also cover the 'cannot read store: <path>' paths (invalid JSON, non-object JSON, failed read leaving the file untouched), which the required-coverage list did not mention. The relative path echo ('.kv.json') is asserted as typed.
'--ttl 0' is used as an extra deterministic expiry check: expiresAt equals the set process's now and isExpired uses <=, so the next process always sees it as expired without sleeping.
Test file split by concern (commands, errors, store-file/atomicity, ttl); all temp state is under os.tmpdir() and no test spawns the CLI with the project directory as cwd.

projectEvents.note: core-cli: implemented bin/kv.js, src/cli.js, src/store.js exactly per the design. Details later tasks may rely on when writing tests/docs: (1) error precedence is usage/exit-2 first (unknown command, wrong arity, --ttl on a non-set command, missing/empty flag value), then key validation ('invalid key: <key>', 1), then ttl validation ('invalid ttl: <value>', 1); (2) loadStore maps any non-ENOENT read failure (not just invalid JSON) to code ESTOREFORMAT so the CLI prints 'cannot read store: <path>' and exits 1 instead of a stack trace; (3) the file path is passed to fs as the user typed it, so messages echo that path (relative '.kv.json' stays relative); (4) an empty-string flag value counts as missing → usage exit 2; (5) repeated --file/--ttl: last occurrence wins; (6) del on an expired key deletes the entry, saves, then prints 'not found: <key>' and exits 1; (7) an empty value is storable via `set key ""`.

projectEvents.summary: Implemented the whole kv CLI, exactly to the frozen design, in the three files in my scope: src/store.js (KEY_PATTERN, isValidKey, emptyStore, isExpired, loadStore, saveStore, pruneExpired, listKeys), src/cli.js (USAGE, run(argv, { now = Date.now() }) returning 0/1/2, main(argv) assigning process.exitCode), and bin/kv.js (shebang, one import, main()). Synchronous ESM only, no dependencies, no process.exit(), no async/await. Argument parsing is a single left-to-right pass where --file and --ttl each consume the next token and every other token (including ones starting with '-') is positional. set joins the remaining arguments with single spaces, prunes expired entries and saves atomically; get prints the value or reports 'not found: <key>' on stderr with exit 1 after removing an expired entry; del prints 'deleted' or the same not-found error; list prints sorted non-expired keys and never writes. Writes go through saveStore: mkdir -p the parent, write JSON.stringify(store, null, 2) + '\n' to <basename>.tmp-<pid>-<random> in the same directory, rename over the target, unlink the temp file on failure. Verified with the five harness acceptance commands (all exit 0) plus 119 ad-hoc assertions across spawned CLI runs and direct module-level checks with an injected fake clock.
openIssues: test/, package.json's scripts.test and README.md are owned by other tasks (cli-tests, readme), so `npm test` does not exist yet from my side; my verification used spawned CLI runs and direct module imports instead. The implementation is ready for the cli-tests suite to exercise.
I did not chmod the executable bit check into any test, and no .kv.json was left behind, so cli-tests can safely spawn the CLI with any working directory.
